analysis|02-25|1956|Η μυστική ομιλία του Χρουστσόφ|Khrushchev's secret speech|After Stalin's death in 1953 the Soviet Union was in a transitional period, with successive changes in leadership and a search for a new political direction. Citizens were still affected by the years of repression, and the party leadership faced internal disputes. Nikita Khrushchev was the leading figure of the era. // On 25 February 1956, at a closed session of the 20th Congress of the Communist Party, Khrushchev denounced Stalin's crimes and cult of personality. The speech was not officially published, but its content quickly leaked to the West and to other countries. The session caused shock among the party members. // The speech opened the way to a partial de-Stalinisation, but also to crises in the Soviet satellite states, such as Hungary in the same year. The history of the speech is regarded as a milestone in the history of the Soviet system. The debate about Stalin and his responsibilities continues to this day. This speech marked a landmark in the revision of Soviet history. Its content is still studied by historians and politicians. The speech opened debates within the party leadership itself and in the societies of Eastern Europe, which saw in it the beginning of change.

analysis|02-25|1986|Ο Μάρκος φεύγει από τις Φιλιππίνες|Marcos leaves the Philippines|In the mid-1980s the Philippines was under the authoritarian regime of Ferdinand Marcos, who had governed since 1965. The economy was in crisis, corruption was rife, and the opposition, led by Corazon Aquino, was calling for democratic elections. Society was polarised and anxious. // After the popular "EDSA" revolution and demonstrations across the country, Marcos was forced to leave the country on 25 February 1986, with the help of the United States. Corazon Aquino took over the presidency and led the transition to democracy. The change came with relatively little violence. // This revolution became a model for the popular mobilisations of the era, and the return to democracy in the Philippines is regarded as successful. However, social and political challenges remained, and the memory of the period is still discussed. The event remains a point of reference for the process of democratisation in Asia. This change affected the functioning of institutions and the relationship of the state with the army. The development was closely followed by international observers. The removal of the president and the return to democracy was a complex process, which required compromises between different political forces and the army.

analysis|02-25|1991|Διαλύεται η στρατιωτική δομή του Συμφώνου της Βαρσοβίας|The military structure of the Warsaw Pact is dissolved|In the early 1990s Eastern Europe had already changed politically, with the fall of the communist regimes in 1989. The Warsaw Pact, the military alliance of the Soviet satellites, was in question, since the member states now sought their own political direction. The USSR was still powerful but weakening. // On 25 February 1991, in Budapest, the member states agreed to end the military structure and the cooperation of the Pact. The decision meant that the military alliance, which had existed since 1955, ceased to function as a unified system of defence. The agreement was treated as an important step towards the easing of tensions in Europe. // The dissolution of the Pact opened the way to a new security architecture for Europe, and to the accession of many former communist countries to NATO and the European Union. The event is regarded as one of the important milestones of the end of the Cold War. The decision was a symptom of the collapse of the Soviet system in Europe. The dissolution of the Pact opened the way to new European alliances. The breakup of the alliance had a symbolic character for the end of the division of Europe, and the following years brought significant changes to borders and alliances.

analysis|02-26|1815|Ο Ναπολέων δραπετεύει από την Έλβα|Napoleon escapes from Elba|After his defeat in Russia and at Leipzig, Napoleon had been exiled to the island of Elba in 1814, while keeping the title of emperor. The European powers had taken on the settlement of borders at the Congress of Vienna, and French public opinion was divided over the restoration of the Bourbons. Napoleon followed developments from his exile. // On 26 February 1815 Napoleon escaped from Elba with a small group of loyalists and returned to France. His return provoked intense reaction in the governments of Europe, but also enthusiasm among part of the French people and the army. The Bourbons were unable to resist. // The period that followed is known as the Hundred Days, and it ended with Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo in June 1815. The development affected the reorganisation of Europe after the Napoleonic wars. The escape remains a symbol of the inability of his opponents to anticipate his moves, and of the complex politics of the era. This escape changes the image of Napoleon as a leader who kept the ability to return to politics. Historians examine it as part of the wider European reorganisation.

analysis|02-26|1929|Ιδρύεται το εθνικό πάρκο Γκραντ Τέτον|Grand Teton National Park is founded|At the beginning of the twentieth century nature conservation in the United States took its first important steps, with the founding of national parks to preserve rare landscapes. The Grand Teton area in Wyoming, with its high peaks and lakes, had attracted the attention of ecologists and travellers. The debate on protecting the area had been active for years. // On 26 February 1929 President Calvin Coolidge signed the law that founded Grand Teton National Park. The area was protected as a natural refuge, with restrictions on activities that could harm the environment. The decision followed other nature protection initiatives of the period. // The park is today an important destination for visitors, and the history of its founding is regarded as a milestone in the management of national parks in the United States. The protection of these areas is linked with the wider debate on the relationship of humans with the natural environment. The decision is still studied as an example of environmental policy. The founding of the park became a model for other areas that would be protected later. The area continues to be an important destination for visitors from all over the world.

analysis|02-26|1936|Το πραξικόπημα της 26ης Φεβρουαρίου|The February 26 coup|In the 1930s Japan was in economic crisis, with rural poverty and political conflicts between the parties and the army. Part of the army demanded a more aggressive policy in Asia and held the parliamentary process in contempt. Young officers believed that politicians and the big businesses had betrayed the nation. // On 26 February 1936 a group of young officers attacked the centre of Tokyo and assassinated several ministers and senior officials. The soldiers occupied government buildings and demanded the overthrow of the government. The coup was violent but did not have the support of the highest military command. // After a few days the movement was suppressed, and its leaders were executed or sentenced. Despite its failure, the event strengthened the influence of the army on politics, since the government became more vulnerable to military demands. This development was linked with the strengthening of Japan's aggressive foreign policy in the following years. This coup changed the balance between the government and the army. This development is linked with Japan's decisions in the 1930s. The military intervention in politics gave new impetus to Japan's aggressive foreign policy and opened the way to the decisions of the following years of the decade.

analysis|02-26|1993|Η βομβιστική επίθεση στο Παγκόσμιο Κέντρο Εμπορίου|The bomb attack on the World Trade Center|In the early 1990s the World Trade Center in New York was one of the most important buildings in the city, with thousands of workers and daily traffic. The security of the buildings was then limited, mainly as regards the garages and vehicle entrances. The city authorities were concerned with strengthening security measures. // On 26 February 1993 a van loaded with explosives exploded in the underground garage of the Twin Towers, killing six people and wounding hundreds. The blast created a large crater and caused smoke and panic in the buildings. The attack was treated as a terrorist act, and an investigation was opened into the perpetrators. // The event became the first major terrorist strike against the Twin Towers, and it led to stricter security measures in buildings and airports. The perpetrators were arrested and tried, and the case remained as a warning about the dangers of the era. The memory of the attack is later linked with the events of 2001. This attack strengthened discussions about the overall protection of large buildings. The security measures that were applied became part of the daily operation of the buildings. The analysis of the responsibilities and of the defensive measures led to revisions of the security rules for large-scale buildings in many countries of the world.

analysis|02-26|1993|Βόμβα στους Δίδυμους Πύργους|Bomb at the Twin Towers|In the early 1990s the American authorities faced new forms of terrorism, and the World Trade Center was one of the symbols of the economic power of the United States. The security of the buildings had been reviewed, but the underground areas remained relatively vulnerable. The debate on protecting citizens was active. // A truck loaded with explosives blew up in the underground car park of the Centre on 26 February 1993, killing six people and injuring many others. The explosion caused damage to the floors and a power cut, but the Twin Towers did not collapse. Rescue workers tried for hours to help those trapped. // The attack left deep marks on American public opinion and prompted new security measures for large buildings. The investigation led to convictions of those involved, and the case was studied as a warning. This attack remains a key event in the history of terrorism in the United States before 2001. The bomb changed the debate on the danger of terrorism in American society. The analysis of the event remains important for security experts. The discussion on terrorism became more intense, and the court proceedings that followed became a field of study for the legal issues of the era.

analysis|02-27|1860|Η ομιλία του Λίνκολν στο Κούπερ Ιούνιον|Lincoln's speech at Cooper Union|In the mid-nineteenth century slavery and its extension into the new territories had become the central issue of American politics. Abraham Lincoln, a politician from Illinois, was relatively unknown on the East Coast, and the Republicans were looking for a candidate who would strengthen their chances of victory. The political debate was intense. // On 27 February 1860 Lincoln spoke at Cooper Union in New York, in a speech that analysed the historical arguments about slavery and argued that the Fathers of the Constitution regarded slavery as something that should be restricted. The speech was well documented and measured, and it became widely known. // The speech made him recognisable to northern voters and helped his candidacy, which led to his election as president the same year. The text is regarded as important for the political thought of the era and for the formation of Republican identity. The speech remains part of the history of anti-slavery politics in the United States. This speech is a text for the study of American political rhetoric. Its measured argumentation continues to be taught at universities. This speech became a point of reference for those who study the history of political ideas and of opposition to slavery in American public discourse.

analysis|02-27|1900|Ιδρύεται το Εργατικό Κόμμα|The Labour Party is founded|At the end of the nineteenth century Britain was experiencing the rise of the labour movement, with trade unions that were growing and demanding better working conditions and political representation. The unions saw that the parties of the era did not adequately express the interests of workers. Socialist groups also operated, but they were divided. // On 27 February 1900 the Labour Representation Committee was formed, with the participation of trade unions and socialist groups, with the aim of electing working-class MPs to Parliament. This committee formed the nucleus from which the Labour Party later emerged. Its founding marked a new phase in British politics. // The Labour Party developed into one of Britain's two major political forces, and its history is linked with the expansion of social rights and of the welfare state. The committee of 1900 is regarded as the starting point for this development. Its history remains a point of reference for the relationship between the labour movement and parliamentary politics. This party went on to become Britain's basic political force in the twentieth century. Its history is studied as an example of the cooperation between trade unions and politics. The creation of the party was linked with the formation of a new political landscape, in which workers' representatives could voice their demands in Parliament.

analysis|02-27|1932|Ο Τσάντγουικ ανακοινώνει το νετρόνιο|Chadwick announces the neutron|In the early 1930s the physics of the atomic nucleus was in full development, with experiments that revealed new particles and phenomena. Scientists knew that the nucleus contains positively charged particles, but the existence of a neutral particle of similar mass was still a matter of debate. Many research centres sought to solve this problem. // On 27 February 1932 the British physicist James Chadwick announced the discovery of the neutron, the neutral particle of the nucleus. The announcement was based on experiments in which atoms were bombarded and on measurements that showed the behaviour of the new particles. The discovery was quickly accepted by the scientific community. // The neutron became the key to understanding the structure of the atom and to the development of nuclear physics. The discovery opened the way to fission and to the applications of nuclear energy, with consequences that affected the strategy and technology of the twentieth century. Chadwick was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935. The discovery of the neutron contributed to the development of atomic physics. Its history is discussed in universities as an example of scientific cooperation. The discovery changed the picture of the composition of the nucleus, and the new measurements provided the basis for later scientific achievements, such as the development of nuclear energy.

analysis|02-27|1933|Η πυρκαγιά του Ράιχσταγκ|The Reichstag fire|In early 1933 Germany was in deep political crisis, with Hitler having become chancellor a few weeks earlier. The democratic Weimar Republic had been weakened, and the Nazi Party was seeking ways to consolidate its power. Political violence was frequent, and Hitler's opponents faced persecution. // On 27 February 1933 a fire broke out in the building of the German parliament in Berlin, the Reichstag. Marinus van der Lubbe, a Dutch communist, was arrested as the alleged perpetrator. The regime used the event to announce a decree that restricted political freedoms. // The decree allowed the Nazis to arrest political opponents without a judicial process and to consolidate their control of power. The fire and its consequences are regarded as one of the important steps towards dictatorship. Historians still debate whether the Nazis were responsible for the fire, but its political result is undeniable. The fire was examined by judicial and historical inquiries, which are still debated. The assessment of the era shows how a crisis can be used to justify the abolition of rights. The assessment of the events was strengthened by testimonies and documents, but the exact responsibility is still debated. The episode remains a point of reference for the relationship between crisis and the suppression of freedoms.

analysis|02-27|1951|Η 22η τροπολογία περιορίζει τις θητείες των προέδρων|The 22nd Amendment limits presidential terms|After Franklin Roosevelt was elected for four consecutive terms, which ended with his death in 1945, the question of a limit on terms became a central debate in Congress. The tradition set by Washington had established a natural limit of two terms, but it was not legally binding. Many politicians demanded the constitutional enshrinement of the limit. // On 27 February 1951 the 22nd Amendment was ratified, providing that no one may be elected President of the United States more than twice. The provision limited the possibility of long presidencies and established the two-term rule at constitutional level. The amendment was treated as an important institutional change. // The 22nd Amendment remains in force, and the debate on term limits recurs often in American politics. Its history shows how institutional changes can affect the dynamics of power in a democracy. The event is regarded as a milestone in the development of the American Constitution. This amendment changed the way American society thinks about power. The debate on the limits of terms returns in every election period. The discussion returned in later periods, with proposals to change the limit, and the 22nd Amendment remains the main legal text on the subject.

analysis|02-28|1922|Η Αίγυπτος γίνεται ανεξάρτητη|Egypt becomes independent|After the First World War Egypt, which had been under British influence since 1882, saw strong nationalist movements. The uprising of 1919, led by Saad Zaghloul, had shown the strong desire of the Egyptians for full independence. Britain was hesitant, but the situation was becoming more and more difficult. // On 28 February 1922 Britain unilaterally declared the independence of Egypt, although the declaration was limited. Britain retained control of defence, communications, minorities and the Suez Canal, while Egypt formally acquired the right to govern itself. The decision opened a new period of negotiations. // This partial independence did not fully satisfy the Egyptians, and the negotiations lasted for years. Full independence and the withdrawal of British troops came in the end after the Second World War and the revolution of 1952. The day of 1922 is regarded as the starting point of the modern Egyptian state. This declaration opened the way to the modern organisation of the Egyptian state. Its history is studied as an example of the gradual transition from colonial rule to independence. This process linked Egyptian identity with the social and political changes of the twentieth century, and the date is honoured as an important milestone of the country.

analysis|02-28|1948|Τα τελευταία βρετανικά στρατεύματα φεύγουν από την Ινδία|The last British troops leave India|The British Empire had ruled India for almost two centuries, first through the East India Company and then directly from London. From the early twentieth century the independence movement had become mass, with leaders such as Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru demanding self-government by peaceful means. The colonial administration, however, continued to control the army, taxation and the basic infrastructure of the country. // India became independent in 1947, but the process was not smooth, since the country was partitioned into two states, India and Pakistan. The movement of millions of people, with violence and massacres, marked the transition. For a time, the British units that were needed to complete the handover of power and the security of the borders remained in the country. Their presence was gradually reduced, and the departure of the last phase marked the end of the direct colonial military presence. // The new India organised a democratic system with its own constitution and institutions, but it faced great problems, such as poverty, religious tensions and the conflict with Pakistan over Kashmir. The departure of foreign forces remained in collective memory as a symbol of final liberation. The event opened the way to the role that India plays today as one of the largest democracies in the world.

analysis|02-28|1953|Οι Γουάτσον και Κρικ ανακαλύπτουν τη δομή του DNA|Watson and Crick discover the structure of DNA|In the early 1950s biologists knew that DNA carries heredity, but it was not clear how it stores and transmits information. In London Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins had gathered X-ray diffraction images, which suggested a helical structure, but the exact model remained unknown. This search was the central question of the era for biology. // In Cambridge James Watson and Francis Crick competed to find the correct arrangement of the chemical components. Using molecular models and the data of other researchers, they found that two chains of nucleotides wind around each other. The bases pair up, adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine, which explained how information is copied. // The discovery opened the way to molecular biology, to the deciphering of the genetic code and to modern techniques of genetic engineering. In 1962 Watson, Crick and Wilkins were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, while Franklin, who had died earlier, was not included. The history of the discovery is still discussed as an example of cooperation, of access to data, and of the recognition of women's contribution to science.

analysis|02-28|1986|Δολοφονείται ο Όλοφ Πάλμε|Olof Palme is assassinated|Olof Palme was the leader of the Swedish Social Democratic Party and had served as prime minister in two periods. On the international stage he supported disarmament diplomacy and non-alignment during the Cold War, which earned him many critics and admirers. The country was regarded as one of the calmest and safest states in Europe, which is why the attack was shocking. // On 28 February 1986 Palme came out of a cinema in Stockholm with his wife and, as they walked along the street, he was shot from behind. He was mortally wounded, while his wife survived with injuries. The police examined many lines of inquiry and a suspect was tried, but he was acquitted on appeal, and the case remained open. // The murder shocked Sweden and left unsolved one of the best-known unsolved crimes in Europe. The case brought to the fore discussions about the safety of politicians and about transparency in the functioning of the police. Palme remains an important figure in Swedish political history, and the absence of an answer about the perpetrator keeps the debate alive.

analysis|02-28|1991|Τερματίζεται ο πόλεμος του Κόλπου|The Gulf War ends|In August 1990 Saddam Hussein's Iraq invaded Kuwait, and the UN demanded an immediate withdrawal. A coalition led by the United States, with a mandate from the Security Council, formed an army with the participation of many states of the region and of the West. The air bombardment began in January 1991, and the ground operation followed. // The ground operations lasted only a few days and led to the rapid collapse of Iraqi forces in Kuwait and in southern Iraq. The ceasefire, announced by the United States at the end of February, brought the fighting to an end, and Kuwait was liberated. Many Iraqi units escaped, while Hussein remained in power. // The Gulf War restored the sovereignty of Kuwait, but it left in place the regime of Hussein, which was overthrown only in 2003. The sanctions against Iraq deeply affected the lives of ordinary people. The conflict showed the power of modern technology in war and opened a period of frequent international interventions in the Middle East.

analysis|02-28|2013|Παραιτείται ο Πάπας Βενέδικτος ΙΣΤ΄|Pope Benedict XVI resigns|Benedict XVI, the German theologian Joseph Ratzinger, had been elected pope in 2005 after the death of John Paul II. During his pontificate he faced great challenges, such as the crisis of trust caused by cases of sexual abuse by clergy and internal disputes within the Roman Curia. Over the years his physical condition deteriorated, and his ministry demanded more and more energy. // On 11 February 2013 he announced that he would resign, citing a lack of bodily and spiritual strength to carry out the office. He set his departure for 28 February, and from then on he held the title of pope emeritus. It was the first voluntary resignation of a pope in almost six centuries, since Gregory XII resigned in 1415. // The decision opened a debate about the length of papal terms and about the coexistence of a retired predecessor with the new pope. The election of Francis followed in March 2013. The resignation remains a rare historical event, showing that the Catholic Church can adapt its procedures without changing its fundamental doctrines.

analysis|02-29|1916|Η Βρετανία προσαρτά το Τοκελάου|Britain annexes Tokelau|Tokelau is a group of small coral islands in the central Pacific, with a few thousand inhabitants and a traditional social organisation. At the beginning of the twentieth century British influence had extended over many Pacific islands, and the small population of Tokelau could not influence the decisions of the great powers. The area thus fell within the sphere of colonial administration. // In 1916 the islands were incorporated into British territory, as part of the administration of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands. The incorporation took place without real participation by the inhabitants, who continued to live according to their customs. Administration was exercised from a distance, with limited presence on the ground. // Responsibility for the islands later passed to New Zealand, and today Tokelau is a dependent territory with internal self-government. Its history shows how even very small islands of the ocean changed sovereignty through diplomatic decisions, without their opinion always being taken into account. The date recalls the expansion of the British Empire in the Pacific.

analysis|02-29|1940|Οκτώ Όσκαρ για το «Όσα Παίρνει ο Άνεμος»|Eight Oscars for Gone with the Wind|In 1940 the film "Gone with the Wind" was one of the greatest successes of American cinema, with an impressive production and dramatic themes about the American South before the Civil War. The film was based on the novel by Margaret Mitchell and marked the era of Hollywood. The depiction of African Americans provoked debate and objections from the time of its release. // At the Academy Awards ceremony the film won eight statuettes, among them the award for best picture and for best actress. Hattie McDaniel became the first African American actress to be honoured with an Oscar, for her role in the category of best supporting actress. The moment was historic, although she herself continued to work within limited opportunities and stereotypes. // The distinction remains in film history as a landmark in the recognition of African American artists, although the path towards real equality in Hollywood was still long. The film remains today a controversial but historically important work, used to discuss the representations of the past in cinema.

analysis|02-29|1960|Ο σεισμός του Αγκαντίρ|The Agadir earthquake|On 29 February 1960 a powerful earthquake struck the city of Agadir, on the Atlantic coast of Morocco, shortly before midnight. The city was densely populated, and most of the buildings had not been designed for earthquakes of such intensity. The area had experienced earlier earthquakes, but the danger was not widely understood. // The earthquake destroyed much of the city within a few seconds, and many families were lost beneath the rubble. Rescue efforts were hampered by destroyed roads and a lack of means. Estimates of the number of dead vary, but they exceed several thousand. // The disaster led to the reconstruction of the city with new anti-seismic design standards and to a radical restructuring of its urban fabric. The event remained in the memory of the residents and gave rise to broader studies of seismic hazard in Morocco and in the Mediterranean. The earthquake is still regarded as one of the most important natural disasters of the twentieth century in the region.

analysis|03-01|1811|Ο Μωχάμετ Αλί σκοτώνει τους Μαμελούκους|Muhammad Ali kills the Mamluks|In the early nineteenth century Egypt was formally an Ottoman province, but real power lay in the hands of the Mamluks, powerful military groups with their own economic base. Muhammad Ali, an Albanian officer who had taken over the administration in 1805, sought to concentrate power in his own hands and to create a modern army. Tension with the old ruling class had escalated for years. // On 1 March 1811 Muhammad Ali invited the Mamluk leaders to a ceremony inside the Citadel of Cairo. As soon as they entered, the gates were closed and a massacre followed. The operation almost completely wiped out their leadership, and those who had escaped were unable to regain their former position. // The act consolidated Muhammad Ali's absolute power and laid the foundations for the dynasty that governed Egypt until the middle of the twentieth century. With the army and the administration being rebuilt on European models, the country changed profoundly in the following decades. The episode is regarded as a turning point in the political history of nineteenth-century Egypt.

analysis|03-01|1896|Η μάχη της Αδούα|The Battle of Adwa|At the end of the nineteenth century the newly unified Italy sought to acquire colonies in Africa, in order to compete with the older European empires. Ethiopia was one of the very few independent states on the continent, with a strong state under Menelik II, who had unified much of the country. Italian influence was growing through agreements, and a treaty was interpreted differently by the two sides, which led to conflict. // On 1 March 1896, near the town of Adwa, the Ethiopian army, with many divisions and knowledge of the terrain, attacked the Italian forces, which were dispersed in mountainous country. The battle was a major clash in which the Italians suffered a heavy defeat, with large numbers of dead and prisoners. Ethiopia managed to resist the expansion of a European state that possessed stronger technology. // The victory made Ethiopia a symbol of African resistance against European colonisation. Italy was forced to recognise the country's independence in a treaty signed shortly afterwards, and the borders remained essentially intact. The defeat, however, did not extinguish Italian expansionism, which later led to the invasion of 1935.

analysis|03-01|1919|Το κίνημα της 1ης Μαρτίου|The March 1st Movement|Korea had been under Japanese rule since 1910, when Japan annexed it after years of growing Japanese influence on the peninsula. The colonial administration restricted the freedoms of the Koreans, while their language and culture were treated with suspicion. After the First World War, ideas about the self-determination of peoples strengthened expectations of independence. // On 1 March 1919 demonstrations took place in Seoul and other cities, where a public declaration of independence was read out. The demonstrations, which were largely peaceful at first, spread over several months across the country, with the participation of people from different social strata, students and religious groups. The Japanese authorities responded with brutal repression, with many dead and arrests. // The movement did not achieve immediate independence, but it became a point of reference for Korean nationalism. In the same year a provisional government in exile was set up in Shanghai, which became the core of the resistance. The anniversary of 1 March remains a national holiday in Korea, as a memory of the struggle against colonial rule.

analysis|03-01|1954|Η δοκιμή «Castle Bravo»|The "Castle Bravo" test|After the Second World War the United States and the Soviet Union competed for nuclear supremacy, and the Americans conducted bomb tests in the Pacific. The Marshall Islands, with the Bikini atoll, were used for the tests, while the inhabitants had no real information about the dangers. The calculations for the yield of the bomb proved to be wrong. // On 1 March 1954 the American hydrogen test "Castle Bravo" released far more energy than expected. The radioactive cloud covered inhabited islands and a Japanese fishing boat, called the Lucky Dragon. Local residents and the crew of the vessel were exposed to radiation, and several faced long-term health problems. // The event strengthened the international reaction against nuclear tests and contributed to the signing of the Partial Test Ban Treaty in 1963. In Japan, the case of the fishermen led to mass movements for peace and for the prohibition of nuclear weapons. The test became a symbol of the dangers of the nuclear age.

analysis|03-01|1961|Ο Κένεντι ιδρύει το Σώμα Ειρήνης|Kennedy founds the Peace Corps|In the early 1960s the United States was competing with the Soviet Union for influence over the newly independent countries of Africa, Asia and Latin America. Many of these faced a shortage of teachers and technicians. President John Kennedy wanted to combine international politics with humanitarian aid and development. // The Peace Corps was founded by executive order, an organisation of volunteers who were sent to developing countries to teach, to work on technical projects and to help local communities. The first volunteers took part in education and health programmes, often living within the communities they served. // The Peace Corps still operates today and has sent volunteers to many countries, although its effectiveness has been debated. The idea of volunteer service abroad influenced other organisations as well. The organisation is a characteristic example of the "soft power" policy of the Cold War era.

analysis|03-02|1836|Το Τέξας ανακηρύσσει ανεξαρτησία|Texas declares independence|In the early nineteenth century Texas was a Mexican province, and American settlers had settled there with the permission of the Mexican government. Differences over slavery, taxes and Mexico's centralised authority increased the settlers' discontent. The government of Santa Anna responded with military measures. // On 2 March 1836 an assembly of settlers declared the independence of Texas from Mexico. The declaration came a few days before the fall of the Alamo, where soldiers of Santa Anna defeated the defenders of the fort. The Texans organised a government and an army, and the conflict continued. // The Republic of Texas functioned as an independent state for about a decade, before being annexed by the United States in 1845. The annexation led to the Mexican-American War and determined the borders of the south-west of America. The event remains controversial, since it is linked with the expansion of slavery and with the loss of Mexican territory.

analysis|03-02|1939|Ο Πίος ΙΒ΄ ενθρονίζεται πάπας|Pius XII is enthroned as pope|Pope Pius XI died in February 1939, and the Catholic Church had to elect a new pontiff in a period of intense international uncertainty. Europe was on the threshold of war, with tensions in Germany, Italy and Spain escalating. // On 2 March 1939 Cardinal Eugenio Pacelli was elected, who took the name Pius XII. The new pope was known as an experienced diplomat, with a long career in the Church's relations with governments, and the election took place relatively quickly. // A few months later the Second World War broke out, and his pontificate was largely judged by his attitude towards the conflict. Discussions about how he dealt with the crimes of Nazism and the Holocaust continue, and historians assess his work differently.

analysis|03-02|1969|Πρώτη πτήση του Κόνκορντ|The first flight of Concorde|The supersonic airliner Concorde was developed by France and Britain in cooperation, despite financial difficulties and political objections. The 1950s and 1960s were an era of great expectations for jet aviation, and European governments wanted to show technological power. // The first flight took place on 2 March 1969 from Toulouse airport in France. The test confirmed the basic design features, and the subsequent flights allowed the aircraft to be developed for commercial use. // Concorde began commercial services in 1976 and became a symbol of technological ambition, especially for flights across the Atlantic. The high operating costs, strict environmental rules and the crash of 2000 led to the end of the services in 2003.

analysis|03-03|1585|Εγκαινιάζεται το Τεάτρο Ολίμπικο της Βιτσέντσα|The Teatro Olimpico of Vicenza is inaugurated|In sixteenth-century Vicenza in Italy, interest in ancient architecture and theatre was intense.
